cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Now that we've done all the research into bike-sharing schemes in cities around the

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: world, we need to think about how we're going to organise our report.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: Right. I think we should start by talking about the benefits.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: I mean it's great that so many cities have introduced these schemes where anyone can pick

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: up a bike from dozens of different locations and hire it for a few hours.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: It makes riding a bike very convenient for people.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Yes, but the costs can add up and that puts people on low incomes off in some places.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: I suppose so, but if it means more people in general are cycling rather than driving,

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: then because they're increasing the amount of physical activity they do, it's good for

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: their health

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: OK. But isn't that of less importance?

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: I mean, doesn't the impact of reduced emissions on air pollution have a more significant

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: effect on people's health?

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: Certainly, in some cities bike-sharing had made a big contribution to that.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: And also helped to cut the number of cars on the road significantly.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: Exactly.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: But I'd say it's had less of an impact on noise pollution because there are still loads

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: of buses and lorries around.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: Shall we quickly discuss the recommendations we're going to make?

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: In order to ensure bike-sharing schemes are successful?

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: OK.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Well, while I think it's nice to have really state-of-the art bikes with things like GPS,

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: I wouldn't say they're absolutely necessary.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: But some technical things are really important – like a fully functional app – so people

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: can make payments and book bikes easily.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: Places which haven't invested in that have really struggled.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Good point ...

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Some people say there shouldn't be competing companies offering separate bike-sharing

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: schemes, but in some really big cities, competition's beneficial and anyway one company

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: might not be able to manage the whole thing.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: Right. Deciding how much to invest is a big question.

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: Cities which have opened loads of new bike lanes at the same time as introducing

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: bike-sharing schemes have generally been more successful – but there are examples of

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: successful schemes where this hasn't happened ...

cues.speaker: MY
cues.text: What does matter though – is having a big publicity campaign.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Definitely.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: If people don't know how to use the scheme or don't understand its benefits, they won't

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: use it. People need a lot of persuasion to stop using their cars.
